items.title: Obaigbena, Others: IGP Overrules AIG Jimoh, Suspends ‘Wanted’ Declaration by Police
items.summary: The Inspector-General of Police overruled a decision to declare nine persons, including THISDAY Chairman Nduka Obaigbena, wanted over alleged threats to First Bank's MD. The IGP suspended the wanted declaration and transferred the investigation to the Force Intelligence Department for a thorough and impartial probe.
items.why: Demonstrates the police hierarchy's commitment to due process and fair investigation procedures in high-profile cases involving prominent citizens.

items.title: One injured as gunmen open fire during NDC rally in Edo
items.summary: One person was injured when gunmen opened fire during an NDC rally in Benin City as presidential candidate Peter Obi visited Edo State. Police deployed additional personnel and launched investigations to apprehend the fleeing assailants.
items.why: Raises concerns about political violence and security challenges during the 2027 election campaign period.

items.title: I bought a book on how to have a son – Makinde
items.summary: Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde revealed that he and his wife purchased books and conception kits based on the Shettles theory to conceive a male child after having two daughters. Cultural expectations and pressure from his mother-in-law influenced their decision to have a third child.
items.why: Illustrates how cultural beliefs and family pressure influence reproductive decisions even among educated, prominent Nigerians.

items.title: Cholera: FCT activates emergency operations centre
items.summary: The Federal Capital Territory Administration has activated its Public Health Emergency Operations Centre to combat an ongoing cholera outbreak ahead of the festive season. The centre will coordinate surveillance, case management, and preventive interventions across affected and vulnerable communities.
items.why: Critical for containing disease spread and protecting public health during a period of increased population movement and gatherings.

items.title: Oshoala celebrates new milestone with MSc in International Sports Management
items.summary: Nigerian footballer Oshoala has achieved a new milestone by obtaining a Master's degree in International Sports Management, representing significant personal growth. The qualification provides a foundation for her potential transition into sports administration and management.
items.why: Highlights the importance of athletes investing in education and professional development beyond their playing careers.

items.title: Pochettino vows to turn Man United’s fortunes around
items.summary: New Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino vowed to improve the team's fortunes after a difficult start, including a 4-0 loss to Liverpool and a 2-2 draw with Sporting Lisbon. He emphasized taking responsibility and leveraging fan support to turn results around.
items.why: Significant for Manchester United's season prospects and Pochettino's ability to restore the club to its traditional competitive level.

items.title: Anthropic chief denies wanting humans to ‘surrender’ free will to AI
items.summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has denied allegations that he advocates for humans to surrender free will to artificial intelligence, calling such suggestions absurd. He criticized rival AI leaders for promoting 'AI as a tool' rhetoric without implementing meaningful safeguards in their products.
items.why: Reflects ongoing debate about AI safety, human autonomy, and the responsibility of tech leaders in developing transformative technologies.

items.title: 2026 in review: 10 events that shaped the world
items.summary: A review of 2026 highlights ten major global events including the US capture of Venezuelan leader Maduro, Middle East conflict expansion, the Artemis II Moon mission, and Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo. These events shaped geopolitics, space exploration, and global health in 2026.
items.why: Provides context for understanding major international developments that will influence global affairs and policy in 2027.

items.title: Registered voters now 100m, says Amupitan, INEC Chairman
items.summary: INEC Chairman announced that registered voters now total over 100 million after removing 1.6 million invalid, duplicated and deceased records from the voters' register. The commission conducted cleaning using automated biometric identification and addressed over 311,000 complaints from citizens.
items.why: Critical for ensuring electoral integrity and accurate voter rolls ahead of the 2027 general elections.

items.title: Iranian twins sentenced to death, 25 years in jail over protests
items.summary: Iranian twin sisters Taraneh and Romina Rahimi have been sentenced to death and 25 years imprisonment respectively for their participation in anti-government protests in Iran. The sisters claim their confessions were obtained through torture and severe mistreatment during detention, allegations their family corroborates.
items.why: Highlights concerns about human rights violations and judicial fairness in Iran's handling of political dissent and protest activities.

items.title: UK woman faces trial over silent prayer outside abortion clinic
items.summary: A UK Christian woman, Isabel Vaughan-Spruce, will stand trial in January 2027 for silently praying outside an abortion clinic in Birmingham, facing charges under the Public Order Act 2023. She maintains that silent prayer cannot be a crime and is defending her fundamental rights to freedom of thought and religion.
items.why: Raises important questions about the balance between protecting abortion access and preserving individual freedoms of conscience and religious expression.

items.title: Indonesian daycare chief jailed nine years for child abuse
items.summary: An Indonesian court sentenced daycare foundation head Diyah Kusumastuti to nine years in prison for allowing child abuse at her facility, where toddlers were found bound and neglected. She was also ordered to pay significant fines and restitution to affected families.
items.why: Underscores the need for stronger enforcement of child protection laws and accountability for institutional negligence in childcare facilities.

items.title: 2027: Atiku will lose ground in North-East – Tinubu’s aide
items.summary: President Tinubu's media adviser Daniel Bwala predicted that former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar will lose electoral ground in the North-East ahead of the 2027 presidential election. Bwala expressed confidence that Tinubu will defeat Atiku by a wider margin than in 2023.
items.why: Indicates shifting political dynamics in key regions and provides insight into the 2027 presidential election landscape.

items.title: UCL: PSG’s Enrique hopes to avoid Roma until final
items.summary: Paris Saint-Germain manager Luis Enrique praised AS Roma as their toughest Champions League opponent, expressing hope to avoid them until a potential final. Enrique acknowledged Roma's quality and competitive performances against Europe's elite teams.
items.why: Reflects Roma's emergence as a formidable European force and adds intrigue to the Champions League competition dynamics.

items.title: North Korea’s Kim calls for more ways to fire nuclear weapons
items.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un called for expanding his country's ability to launch nuclear weapons from multiple platforms, emphasizing that nuclear capability is now a constitutional reality. He accused the US of attempting to replicate security pacts in Northeast Asia.
items.why: Demonstrates North Korea's commitment to nuclear expansion and escalates regional security tensions in Northeast Asia.
